body:
Why energy technologies need manufacturing clusters

The expansion of electric mobility, renewable electricity and energy storage creates demand for specialised industrial materials. These technologies connect Gujarat's established chemical and engineering industries with newer electronics and energy-related activities.

It is important to distinguish energy production, energy storage and energy use. A solar photovoltaic panel generates electricity from sunlight. A rechargeable battery stores electrical energy through reversible chemical reactions. An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical motion.

How a rechargeable battery works

A rechargeable battery stores energy through electrochemical reactions. Its basic components include a positive electrode, a negative electrode, an electrolyte and a separator.

During discharge, ions move through the electrolyte while electrons travel through the external circuit to supply electrical power. Charging reverses the relevant electrochemical changes by using an external electrical supply.

In a lithium-ion battery, lithium ions move between electrode materials during charging and discharging. A battery's performance depends on its materials, construction and operating conditions.

Cell, module and pack

A battery cell is the basic electrochemical unit that stores energy. Several cells may be combined into a module, and modules or directly grouped cells may be assembled into a battery pack.

A battery pack generally includes electrical connections and protective equipment. A battery-management system (BMS) monitors and helps manage operating conditions such as voltage, current and temperature.

The distinction matters for industry analysis. A company assembling imported battery cells into packs is not necessarily manufacturing the electrochemical cells themselves.

Materials used in energy-storage supply chains

Battery manufacturing requires electrode materials, electrolytes, separators and suitable electrical connections. Associated industries may supply processed minerals, chemicals, metals, machinery and electronic controls.

Not all rechargeable batteries use identical materials. Lithium-ion, sodium-ion and other battery systems employ different combinations of materials and designs. The term advanced chemistry cell (ACC) is used in India's industrial policy for advanced rechargeable energy-storage cells. It should not be mistaken for an ordinary description of a complete electric vehicle.

India's Advanced Chemistry Cell production incentive programme

The Ministry of Heavy Industries administers the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell Battery Storage. The programme was approved in May 2021 with an outlay of ₹18,100 crore and a target of establishing 50 GWh of domestic ACC manufacturing capacity.

In an official reply dated 10 February 2026, the Ministry identified a 5 GWh award to Reliance New Energy Battery Storage Limited associated with Jamnagar, Gujarat. The capacity figure describes an award under the scheme, not verified cell output.

A subsequent official reply dated 27 March 2026 recorded 0 GWh of installed capacity against that beneficiary's 5 GWh award in the reported implementation snapshot. This is the status reported on that date; it does not establish the project's installation status on 14 November 2026.

Capacity awarded is not capacity installed. A company may receive approval or an incentive-linked award before completing its manufacturing plant. An announced investment, an installed plant and actual commercial production represent different stages.

Green hydrogen and Gujarat's port connection

Hydrogen is an energy carrier: energy must first be used to produce it. Green hydrogen generally refers to hydrogen produced using renewable electricity, commonly through the electrolysis of water.

Electrolysis uses electrical energy to separate water into hydrogen and oxygen. When the electricity comes from qualifying renewable sources, the resulting hydrogen can reduce dependence on fossil-derived hydrogen in suitable applications.

The Government of India approved the National Green Hydrogen Mission on 4 January 2023. Its objectives include developing green-hydrogen production and use, strengthening domestic capabilities and reducing emissions in relevant sectors.

At Deendayal Port Authority, Kandla, a 1 MW green-hydrogen plant was commissioned on 31 July 2025, according to the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. This is an implemented example of the connection between port infrastructure and an emerging energy technology.

Why batteries, hydrogen and solar power are different

TechnologyMain functionImportant distinction
Solar photovoltaic panelGenerates electricity from sunlightDoes not itself provide long-term stored electrical energy
Rechargeable batteryStores and releases electrical energyRequires charging from an external energy source
Green hydrogenCarries energy in chemical formRequires energy for production, usually renewable-powered electrolysis
Electric motorConverts electrical energy into mechanical motionUses electricity rather than storing substantial energy

Recycling and material security

Some battery technologies depend on minerals and processed materials that have concentrated global supply chains. This creates concerns about import dependence, price changes and supply disruption.

Battery recycling can recover useful materials from end-of-life batteries and suitable manufacturing scrap. Recycling does not eliminate the need for new raw materials, but it may reduce waste and the demand for some newly extracted resources. Safe collection and processing are important because batteries can present electrical, thermal and chemical hazards.

Prelims focus

  • A battery cell is the basic electrochemical energy-storage unit; a battery pack combines cells with supporting systems.
  • A battery-management system helps monitor and manage battery operating conditions.
  • India's ACC PLI programme was approved in May 2021 with a 50 GWh capacity target.
  • A 5 GWh ACC award was associated with Jamnagar in the Ministry's February 2026 statement.
  • The National Green Hydrogen Mission was approved on 4 January 2023.
  • Trap: Awarded battery capacity, installed battery capacity and actual production are not equivalent.

[Ministry of Heavy Industries, PLI-ACC Scheme, parliamentary reply dated 10 February 2026, including project locations and data reported as of 31 December 2025; Ministry of Heavy Industries, ACC Battery Production-Linked Incentive Scheme, parliamentary reply dated 27 March 2026, beneficiary commissioning-status table; Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Cabinet Approval of National Green Hydrogen Mission, 4 January 2023; Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Indigenously Built 1 MW Green Hydrogen Plant Commissioned at Kandla Port, 31 July 2025; official materials consulted 14 November 2026.]

body:
Manufacturing supply chains are interconnected

Gujarat's manufacturing economy combines established industries with newer technology-oriented activities. Ceramic factories require minerals, machinery and fuel. Automobile manufacturers require metal and plastic components. Semiconductor facilities require specialised chemicals, precision equipment and reliable utilities. Battery manufacturers require processed materials, chemicals and electrical components.

The industries therefore create opportunities for one another. Their connections are based on actual material, component and service requirements rather than geographical proximity alone.

Important industrial-development terms

Different terms are used for planned industrial areas and supporting government programmes. They describe different purposes.

TermMeaningGujarat connection
Industrial clusterGeographical concentration of related enterprises and servicesMorbi ceramics; Jamnagar brass; Rajkot engineering
GIDC industrial estateOrganised industrial area developed or managed through GIDCIndustrial estates at locations including Sanand, Dahej and Ankleshwar
Special Investment Region (SIR)Designated region planned for large-scale investment and infrastructure developmentDholera and Mandal–Becharaji
PCPIRRegion intended to support petroleum, chemical and petrochemical industriesDahej, Bharuch
Special Economic Zone (SEZ)Designated area operating under the applicable SEZ legal and regulatory framework; deemed outside India's customs territory for authorised operationsNotified SEZ for the Dholera semiconductor project in April 2026

These descriptions can overlap geographically without becoming synonyms. A semiconductor project may be located within a Special Investment Region and also receive SEZ status. The 2 designations refer to different planning or regulatory functions.

What government programmes do

  • GIDC: Supports organised industrial development through estates, land and infrastructure-related services.
  • Gujarat Semiconductor Policy (2022–27): Provides a state policy framework intended to attract eligible semiconductor and display-related projects.
  • Gujarat Electronics Policy (2022–28): Supports the development of electronics manufacturing and its associated ecosystem.
  • Gujarat Electronics Component Manufacturing Policy (2025): Addresses the expansion of electronics-component and related manufacturing capabilities.
  • India Semiconductor Mission: Supports the development of India's semiconductor and display ecosystem.
  • ACC PLI Scheme: Encourages eligible domestic advanced battery-cell manufacturing capacity.
  • National Green Hydrogen Mission: Promotes the development of green hydrogen and its applications.

A policy may provide incentives or an enabling framework. Its announcement does not demonstrate that every proposed industrial unit has been constructed or commissioned.

Different industries create different environmental challenges

Manufacturing requires careful management of resources and waste. The appropriate measures depend on the sector.

IndustryImportant concernGeneral response
CeramicsKiln energy use and dustEnergy efficiency and dust control
ChemicalsHazardous substances and industrial effluentsSafe handling and appropriate treatment
Foundries and engineeringFurnace emissions and metal wasteEmission control and suitable material recovery
Automobiles and batteriesMaterial consumption and end-of-life wasteReuse, recycling and safe disposal
SemiconductorsHigh-quality utility requirements and specialised process wasteCareful utility management and appropriate waste treatment

The Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) has responsibilities connected with preventing and controlling pollution in the state. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) promotes more efficient energy use. Their functions differ: pollution control addresses harmful environmental releases, while energy efficiency reduces the energy required to obtain a given output.

One-glance revision of the main industrial locations

The principal associations can be recalled through the products or activities for which each location is important:

  • Morbi: Ceramic tiles, including vitrified tiles, and other ceramic products.
  • Thangadh: Sanitaryware and refractory ceramics.
  • Rajkot: Engineering goods, foundries and machinery-related components.
  • Jamnagar: Brass engineering and a separate major petroleum-refining industry.
  • Vadodara, Nandesari, Ankleshwar and Dahej: Important chemical and petrochemical activities.
  • Sanand, Mandal–Becharaji and Halol: Automobile manufacturing and related suppliers.
  • Sanand: Semiconductor assembly, testing and packaging facilities that reached commercial production during 2026.
  • Dholera: Tata Electronics–PSMC semiconductor wafer-fabrication project under development at the selected cutoff.
  • Kandla: Port-related green-hydrogen development, including a 1 MW plant commissioned in July 2025.

Understanding statements about industrial projects

When comparing industrial developments, the status of a project is as important as its name and location.

  • Proposed: A project has been put forward but may still require approvals, finance or construction.
  • Approved or notified: A required official decision has been made. This does not itself establish production.
  • Under construction: Physical facilities are being developed, but the full planned production activity may not yet have started.
  • Pilot operation: A limited operation is being used to develop or demonstrate production capability.
  • Commercial production: The enterprise has begun producing for commercial use or supply.

For example, the approval of the Dholera semiconductor project in 2024, its SEZ notification in 2026 and the commercial production achieved by certain Sanand packaging facilities in 2026 are separate facts. They describe different projects or different stages of development.

Prelims focus

  • Morbi–ceramics, Rajkot–engineering and Jamnagar–brass are important industrial associations.
  • Dahej in Bharuch district is associated with the PCPIR.
  • Sanand is associated with both automobile manufacturing and semiconductor packaging.
  • Dholera is associated with a semiconductor wafer-fabrication project under development.
  • GIDC, GPCB and BEE perform different functions related to industrial infrastructure, pollution control and energy efficiency.
  • Trap: A project announcement, an approval, a notified industrial zone and commercial production are not equivalent milestones.

[NCERT, Class 8 Geography, Resources and Development, Chapter 5, Industries, printed pp. 50–52; NCERT, Class 11 Economics, Indian Economic Development, Chapter 8, Infrastructure, printed pp. 140–143; Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation, Industrial Estate Directory and Integrated Ceramic Park brochure, 2024 and FY 2026–27 materials; Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, PCPIR implementation information; Government of Gujarat, Department of Science and Technology, semiconductor and electronics policy documents dated 2022 and 2025; Press Information Bureau, semiconductor facility announcements dated 28 February, 31 March, 16 April, 4 July and 28 September 2026; Bureau of Energy Efficiency, selected MSME cluster information; sources consulted 14 November 2026.]
